answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to post a refundable bond before it may whisper offers into the harbor’s shared order book. Reputation then accrues only from completed trades with distinct, already bonded counterparties, not from self-dealing among accounts controlled by one operator. A sybil farm must therefore lock real capital for every identity and risk losing it when it defaults or is caught colluding; the ferrous token is no magic shield, but makes mass identities costly rather than free.
